_note: Inputs come from the `pr_*` tape, INSIDE cuflxn after its first blocks have zeroed the generation outside the cloud, because that is what the sweeps see -- not what cumastrn passed in. References come from the `cx_*` tape at cuflxn's own exit, not the `fx_*` one before cudtdqn (FORTRAN_BUGS N113). `pqsen` is reshaped from the flat dump because cumastrn declares it rank-1 (N110).

tests.description: cuflxn's precipitation sweeps on the chem170 single-column reference, step 1, TILE COLUMN 1 of 2: cloud top at kernel level 5, base at 44, peak rain flux 0.00927 and peak snow flux 0.00789 kg/(m^2 s), peak melting rate 0.00154. The column is named because the two columns of the SCM tile reach different convective outcomes at the same step, so a regime table collapsing to one value per step would hide which was tested. Reference run: data/eqwefic/notes/chem170_scm_reference_run.md (em_scm_xy, Weisman-Klemp sounding over Kansas, dx = 20 km, 59 levels, dt = 60 s, cu_physics = 16). Reference build: the real64 replay through kernels/ntiedtke_driver of WRF fork branch earthsciml-instrumented-chem170, the seven constants cu_ntiedtke_init takes supplied at binary64 precision; the scheme's own literals stay at their binary32 roundings (FORTRAN_BUGS N109). **The values come from the `cx_*` tape, taken at cuflxn's OWN EXIT.** They are NOT the fluxes the next stage sees: cumastrn afterwards rescales the downdraught mass flux and adds the remainder back into the rain, then recomputes the precipitation generation as the flux difference (FORTRAN_BUGS N113). Pinning against the later state disagrees by up to 0.31 of the flux amplitude on exactly the columns whose downdraught was rescaled, and is bit-exact on the rest -- a split that reads as a transcription error and is a wrong reference. Algebraic observeds at t = 0 with no ODE state, so the empty time_span is one static evaluation.
